title: AI drawer: the model picked in the composer falls back to the default after every answer
body:
## What happens

In the console's AI drawer (the side panel opened from the header's assistant icon), pick a non-default model in the composer's model picker (e.g. `Fast - Minmax 3.1 Flash` instead of `Fast · Claude Haiku 5.5`), then ask a question. When the answer finishes, the picker shows the default model again. It happens after **every** answer, not only the first send of a new conversation.

Seen on a deployed console: ObjectStack 19.0.0-next.0, console build `1dbf19a1`, app `ai.objectstack.brightrule`, both on an app `page` (`brightrule_home`) and on a record page. Six models offered (Haiku 5.5 ×1, Deepseek 4.1 Flash ×1, Minmax 3.1 Flash ×1, Qianwen 3.8 Omni Flash ×1, Sonnet 5.5 ×20, Opus 5.5 ×40).

## Why it matters

`ChatPane` sends the value the picker shows (`effectiveModelId = selectedModelId ?? defaultModelId`, `console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx`), so after the reset the next question silently runs on the default model. A user who picked a stronger model for a hard question gets the default one on the follow-up without noticing, and one who picked a cheaper one is charged at the default's multiplier.

## What the code intends

ADR-0028: the pick is held by the host, `ChatDockConversation` (`layout/ChatDockConversation.tsx:216`, "held here so it outlives the keyed pane's remount when the first send mints the conversation"), and handed to the pane as `selectedModelId` / `onSelectedModelChange`. The pane's own key (`${chatApi}:${paneConversationId}`) changing should therefore not lose it. That the pick is still lost after each answer suggests `ChatDockConversation` itself is remounted (or its state reset) around the end of a turn — `handleSent` bumps `refreshKey`, and the drawer mounts the body lazily under `React.Suspense` in `ChatDock.tsx` — but I have not reproduced it locally (no AI service there), so the cause is a guess.

## Expected

The picked model stays picked for the rest of the drawer conversation (and the next request uses it), as on the full-page chat.
